MOMOTHECAT.story: Momo, a solid black cat with yellow eyes, tips her witch's hat and waves her little wand at dusk.
MOMOTHECAT.look: A normal four-legged solid black cat with bright yellow eyes, wearing a small pointed purple witch's hat and holding a little magic wand with a glowing tip in one front paw. No text or logo.
MOMOTHECAT.why: She follows Momo the Cat, the black cat of Google's Halloween Doodle games, drawn from Doodle artist Juliana Chen's real black cat Momo: black coat, yellow eyes, the witch's hat and the glowing wand.

LEOTHELION.story: Leo, a proud lion with a full golden mane, sits on the old sundial and follows the sun.
LEOTHELION.look: A majestic adult male lion with a full, thick golden-brown mane, a tawny body and calm golden eyes, sitting with his head held high as in a classic film-studio lion portrait. No ring, ribbon, text or logo.
LEOTHELION.why: He follows Leo the Lion, the MGM lion now used by Amazon MGM Studios: a real male lion with a full golden-brown mane, head held high. The logo's ring and text are left out.

TUMBLES.name: Olivia Benson
TUMBLES.story: Olivia Benson, a Scottish Fold kitten with folded ears, naps in the garden hammock as more kittens pile in.
TUMBLES.look: A young Scottish Fold kitten with small ears folded flat forward, a round face, a white coat with soft grey tabby markings on the head and back, and big round copper eyes. She wears nothing.
TUMBLES.why: She follows Olivia Benson, the Scottish Fold kitten who co-starred in the Diet Coke 'Kittens' ad announced in Coca-Cola's own 2014 press release: folded ears and a white coat with grey tabby markings (the coat is from general knowledge of the cat; the notes quote only her name).
TUMBLES.src: Coca-Cola press release 2014 on the Diet Coke 'Kittens' ad: 'Taylor's own kitten Olivia Benson' (notes/KOX.md)

SAVEPAWS.story: Save Point, a small brown tabby kitten in a red headband, lets out a big roar before every adventure.
SAVEPAWS.look: A small brown mackerel-tabby kitten roaring fiercely with its mouth wide open, wearing a red cloth headband tied round its forehead with the ends trailing. No text or logo.
SAVEPAWS.why: She follows the kitten avatar of Roaring Kitty, the best-known GME fan account (@TheRoaringKitty): a roaring brown mackerel-tabby kitten in a red headband. No real name was found for the kitten, so the name is unchanged.

PEWTER.story: Pewter, a silver-grey tabby in a green feathered cap and tunic, rolls in the catmint.
PEWTER.look: A normal four-legged grey tabby cat with dark bars on the cheeks, a white chin and a pink nose, dressed as Robin Hood in a pointed green felt cap with a red feather and a belted green tunic. No text or logo.
PEWTER.why: She is the grey tabby pixel cat that @RobinhoodApp posted in Aug-Sep 2026, with its Robin Hood cap, feather and tunic: dark bars on the cheeks, white chin, pink nose. The pixel cat has no official name.

BRACKEN.name: Update Cat
BRACKEN.story: Update Cat, a sturdy grey-brown striped tabby with a black-ringed tail, stalks moths through the ferns at dusk.
BRACKEN.why: Named after Update Cat, the cat of Intel's 2018 #UpdateMeow online-safety campaign. No picture of Update Cat was found, so the look still comes from Intel's 'Wildcat Lake' codename: a wildcat's grey-brown striped coat and a black-ringed tail.
BRACKEN.src: National Cybersecurity Alliance press release 2018-10-31 (Intel + NCSA #UpdateMeow): 'Update Cat - the newest, online safety star' (notes/INTCX.md)
